newsitem.title: HUNGARY: FORECAST-Hungary govt paper yields seen up in Dec.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Hungary govt paper yields seen up in Dec.

text.p: Yields on Hungarian government securities on the secondary market were seen continuing last week's rises, which came as a correction after an almost unbroken fall since January, dealers said.
They added the corrections were also triggered by a continuous flow of new issues on the market where liquidity was tight, as is usual at the end of the year.
"Nobody has money," said Istvan Halasz of Bank Austria Girocredit. "I expect very low turnover and rising yield levels."
Said Zsolt Bango of Gog Securities: "The market has done a U-turn compared with the earlier weeks."
Six-month and 12-month Treasury bill yields on the secondary market rose 0.3 to 0.5 percentage points to 22.3-22.4 percent last week.
Fixed interest government bond yields also rose 0.2 to 0.4 percentage points last week, dealers said.

They added that the yields on discount Treasury bills, which have up to one year maturity, are expected to rise further this week, by up to 0.3 percent, and government bonds were seen following them at a slower pace.

Dealers said the upward corrections were likely to dominate this month, but demand on the market was likely to regain its strength in January, with the yields dropping again to the levels of early December.
Year-on-year inflation, which dropped to 20.1 percent by November from 28.3 in December 1995, pushing down yields and interest rates, was likely to continue to drop next year, dealers said.

But after January, the yields would probably stay steady for at least half a year as Hungary plans to keep its monthly pre-announced devaluation rate at 1.2 percent in the first six months of 1997, dealers added.
